h1: Attic Cleaning in San Leandro, CA
description: Attic cleaning in San Leandro, CA: debris, dust and droppings removed and the space sanitized before new insulation. Get a free inspection and estimate.
intro: We clean and sanitize attics across the East Bay: debris, dust and rodent droppings vacuumed out, the deck and framing treated, and the space left dry and ready for new insulation. Free inspection, fixed written estimate.
hero_alt: Clean sanitized attic deck in an East Bay home

sections.h2: What hides in an old attic
paragraphs: Dust from past remodels, construction debris and droppings from rodents settle into attic insulation and on the deck. None of it belongs under new insulation.
The inspection documents what is up there with photos, so the cleaning scope is based on what we actually saw, not a square-foot formula.
Cleaning means vacuuming out the old material and debris, removing droppings, and sanitizing the deck and framing so the attic is a clean surface for whatever comes next.
bullets: Vacuum removal of debris and damaged insulation
Sanitizing treatment on the deck and framing
Waste bagged and disposed of properly

paragraphs: New insulation over droppings, dust or mold locks the problem into the attic. We clean first, then insulate, so the material goes down on a dry, sanitized surface.
If the cleaning reveals moisture or rodent activity, we flag it before any insulation is scheduled, so the root cause gets fixed instead of covered.
Droppings are evidence of a rodent problem, not just a mess. Before we reinsulate, entry points get sealed so the attic stays clean after we leave.
We do not lay traps or bait. We seal the building so rodents cannot get back in, then clean what they left behind.
A cleaned attic smells neutral, holds insulation properly, and is safer to work in for every trade that follows: electricians, plumbers and HVAC crews.
We leave the space ready for new insulation, with photos so you can see the difference.

faqs.q: Why clean the attic before insulating?
faqs.a: Because new insulation over dust, droppings or mold locks those problems in. A clean, dry surface is what lets insulation do its job for the long term.
Yes. Droppings and nesting material are vacuumed out as part of the cleaning, and we flag the entry points that let the rodents in so they can be sealed.

faqs.q: How long does an attic cleaning take?
faqs.a: Most attics clean up in a day. Heavy debris or large droppings contamination can extend the job, and the estimate states the schedule.
Once the source material is removed and the space is sanitized, the smell fades, usually within days. If it lingers, we re-check for moisture or missed debris.

faqs.q: Can you clean and insulate in the same visit?
faqs.a: Often yes. We clean first, verify the deck is dry, and then new insulation goes in. Both scopes are quoted together as one fixed estimate.

faqs.q: Is the waste disposed of properly?
faqs.a: Yes. Contaminated material is bagged and taken for proper disposal, and it is included in the fixed estimate.
